title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Harvard/Cellular Intelligence study fitting over 2,000 representation models across single-cell transcriptomics, imaging and protein sequences finds measurement noise is a third scaling axis with a universal logarithmic law, parameterized by capacity (I_max) and noise robustness. Single-cell and especially spatial transcriptomic models remain noise-limited at current sequencing depths, protein-sequence models already tolerate sequencing error, and transformer Geneformer trades higher noise robustness for lower capacity than the VAE scVI.

insights.claim: Fitting more than 2,000 representation learning models across gene expression, protein sequence and image data shows measurement noise is a distinct scaling axis for model performance, alongside dataset size and model size.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Biological foundation-model roadmaps that plan only on data volume and parameters are missing a quantifiable lever: measurement quality.
insights.quote: establishing measurement noise as a third, quantifiable scaling axis for representation learning, alongside dataset size and model size
insights.locator: Discussion: In conclusion, across single-cell transcriptomics

insights.claim: Representation-model performance versus measurement signal-to-noise ratio follows a logarithmic law (not a power law), derived from an additive Gaussian noise channel model and parameterized by maximum information I_max and a noise-robustness scale eta-bar.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Gives a two-parameter curve to forecast how much performance extra sequencing/imaging quality buys, analogous to compute scaling laws.
insights.quote: Noise scaling follows a logarithmic law.
insights.locator: Abstract

insights.claim: When 233 noise-scaling curves built from 2,328 fitted models (200 transcriptomic, 33 image and sequence) are rescaled by their fitted parameters, they collapse onto a single universal curve with theory fit R2 = 0.967 +/- 0.004.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Universality across architectures and modalities means the law can be used as a planning tool rather than a model-specific curiosity.

insights.claim: The noise scaling law holds for transcriptomic datasets spanning nearly five orders of magnitude in sample size, across hyperparameter choices and fine-tuning for STATE, and for Geneformer sizes from 0.71M to 54.8M parameters.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Robustness to model size and training regime suggests the law will extrapolate to larger bio foundation models being funded now.

insights.claim: Validation loss is a poor metric for comparing representation models because it is not comparable across loss functions or data with different noise properties, and lower loss need not yield more useful downstream representations.

insights.claim: The authors propose auxiliary mutual information, the MI between a learned representation and a held-out auxiliary signal measured in bits via a neural MI estimator, as a cross-model, cross-noise performance metric that generalizes linear probing.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A standard bits-based metric could become the yardstick for evaluating competing cell-model products.

insights.claim: Auxiliary MI scores agree well with linear-probing goodness of fit, with an average Kendall rank correlation of tau = 0.71, while also capturing nonlinear relationships.

insights.claim: Mutual information with cell-type labels is biased toward whichever embedding was used to annotate those labels, so the study uses independently measured auxiliary signals such as spatial position, clonal identity, surface protein abundance and developmental stage.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Common cell-atlas benchmarks scored on cell-type labels may be circular and overstate the models used to build them.

insights.claim: Probe-based MI is tied to a specific downstream task and ignores variation unrelated to the auxiliary signal, so it is not a universal measure of representation quality.

insights.claim: The MI metric reproduces known sample-size scaling: neural cell models (scVI, Geneformer, STATE) follow a saturating power law in cell number with mean R2 = 0.90 across 120 models, while PCA saturates almost immediately.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Confirms deep models keep extracting value from more cells where linear baselines plateau, supporting large cell-atlas investments.
